name: analytics
description: Analytical workload over the pqgen datasets (scale 1m). Defined by the Rust engine because benchmarks/workloads/analytics.json is not present in the workspace; see README 'Latency optimization'.

queries.name: revenue by category
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount FROM transactions WHERE status = 'approved' GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC

queries.name: monthly trend
queries.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', ts) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS revenue, SUM(fee) AS fees FROM transactions GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', ts) ORDER BY month

queries.name: fraud rate by currency
queries.sql: SELECT currency, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN is_fraud THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS frauds, AVG(CASE WHEN is_fraud THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS fraud_rate FROM transactions GROUP BY currency ORDER BY currency

queries.name: top customers by spend
queries.sql: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS spend, COUNT(*) AS n FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY spend DESC, customer_id LIMIT 20

queries.name: segment x country revenue (join)
queries.sql: SELECT c.segment, c.country, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(t.amount) AS revenue FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.status = 'approved' GROUP BY c.segment, c.country ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.segment, c.country LIMIT 25

queries.name: order gross by status and year (join)
queries.sql: SELECT o.status, YEAR(o.order_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status, YEAR(o.order_date) ORDER BY o.status, yr

queries.name: delivered sales by category/brand (3-way join)
queries.sql: SELECT p.category, p.brand, SUM(i.quantity) AS units, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price - COALESCE(i.discount, 0)) AS net FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY p.category, p.brand ORDER BY net DESC, p.category, p.brand LIMIT 20

queries.name: active-customer country revenue (4-way join)
queries.sql: SELECT c.country, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders, SUM(i.quantity * p.price) AS list_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE c.is_active GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY c.country

queries.name: sensor hourly profile
queries.sql: SELECT status, HOUR(ts) AS h, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(temperature) AS avg_temp, MIN(humidity) AS min_hum, MAX(pressure) AS max_pres FROM sensor_readings GROUP BY status, HOUR(ts) ORDER BY status, h

queries.name: sensor anomalies (filter, having, top-N)
queries.sql: SELECT sensor_id, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(temperature) AS avg_temp FROM sensor_readings WHERE temperature > 30 OR humidity < 15 GROUP BY sensor_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 ORDER BY n DESC, sensor_id LIMIT 50

queries.name: customers with large transactions (IN subquery)
queries.sql: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers c WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM transactions WHERE amount > 2000) GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment

queries.name: customers without orders (correlated NOT EXISTS)
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id)

queries.name: transactions above 3x average (scalar subquery)
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE amount > (SELECT AVG(amount) * 3 FROM transactions)

queries.name: spend per segment (CTE + join)
queries.sql: WITH cust_spend AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS spend FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT c.segment, COUNT(*) AS customers, AVG(s.spend) AS avg_spend, MAX(s.spend) AS max_spend FROM cust_spend s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment

queries.name: distinct merchants/customers per category
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(DISTINCT merchant_id) AS merchants, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers FROM transactions GROUP BY category ORDER BY category

queries.name: string predicates (LIKE, UPPER, SUBSTR)
queries.sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com' AND UPPER(SUBSTR(name, 1, 1)) = 'A' GROUP BY country ORDER BY n DESC, country

queries.name: selective range scan, wide rows
queries.sql: SELECT tx_id, customer_id, merchant_id, amount, currency, category, ts, status FROM transactions WHERE customer_id BETWEEN 1000 AND 1199 ORDER BY tx_id

queries.name: top-100 electronics transactions
queries.sql: SELECT tx_id, customer_id, amount, ts FROM transactions WHERE category = 'electronics' ORDER BY amount DESC, tx_id LIMIT 100

queries.name: deep sort page (multi-key sort + offset)
queries.sql: SELECT str_key, dup_key, id FROM sort_keys ORDER BY str_key, dup_key DESC, id LIMIT 1000 OFFSET 100000

queries.name: product coverage (LEFT JOIN)
queries.sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(i.order_id) AS big_lines, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id AND i.quantity > 8 GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY p.category

queries.name: null-heavy aggregates
queries.sql: SELECT s70, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(n50) AS c50, SUM(n90) AS s90, AVG(f95) AS a95, MIN(d99) AS min_d FROM nulls_heavy WHERE b60 IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s70 ORDER BY s70 NULLS FIRST

queries.name: signup-to-order latency by segment (join, date math)
queries.sql: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(DATE_DIFF('day', c.signup_date, o.order_date)) AS avg_days FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= c.signup_date GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment

queries.name: status summary (UNION ALL)
queries.sql: SELECT 'fraud_tx' AS kind, COUNT(*) AS n FROM transactions WHERE is_fraud UNION ALL SELECT 'returned_orders', COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'returned' UNION ALL SELECT 'bad_sensor', COUNT(*) FROM sensor_readings WHERE status <> 'ok'

queries.name: full-table global aggregates
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS amount, SUM(fee) AS fee, MIN(ts) AS first_ts, MAX(ts) AS last_ts, AVG(bucket) AS avg_bucket FROM transactions
